questions.question: Krishna, Mahesh and Gautam can do a work in 90, 30 and 45 days respectively. If they work together, in how many days will they complete work?
questions.explanation:
Calculation:

Krishna’s one day’s work = \(\frac{1}{90}\)

Mahesh’s one day’s work = \(\frac{1}{30}\)

gautam’s one day’s work = \(\frac{1}{45}\)

Krishna, Mahesh and gautam together can do the work = \(\frac{1}{90} + \frac{1}{30} + \frac{1}{45} = \ \frac{1}{90}(1 + 3 + 2) = \frac{6}{90} = \frac{1}{15}\)

So, they will complete the work in 15 days.

Alternate Method:

LCM of 90, 30, and 45 is 90.

Therefore, Total work = 90

Krishna :  90                  1

Mahesh : 30        90      3

Gautam : 45                  2

The efficiency of Krishna, Mahesh, and Gautam is 1, 3, and 2, respectively.

Total days required to complete the work = 90/6 = 15 days

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 3 days and B can do it in 2 days . How much time will be taken by them to do the work together ?(days)
questions.explanation:
LCM(2,3)=6
Let work to be done be 6 units.

Work done by A in 1 day\(= \frac{6}{3} = 2\ units\)

Work done by B in 1 day \(= \frac{6}{2} = 3\ units\)

Time taken by them to complete the work \(= \frac{6}{2 + 3} = 1.2\ days\)

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 4 hours , B and C can do it in 3 hours . A and C can do it in 2 hours . How long will B alone take to do it ?
questions.explanation:
LCM (4,3,2)\(= 12\ units\)

Let total work to be done be 12 units.

Work done by ;

A in a day\(\  = \ \frac{12}{4} = 3\ units—(1)\)

B+C in a day \(= \ \frac{12}{3} = \ 4\ units–(2)\)

A+C in a day \(= \ \frac{12}{2} = \ 6\ units—(3)\)

Putting (1) in (3)

\(3 + C = 6\)

\( C\  = \ 3\ units\)

Putting C in (2);

\(3 + B = 4\)

\( B\  = \ 1\ units\)

TIme taken by B \(= \ \frac{12}{1} = \ 12\ hours\)

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 6 hours ; B and C can do it in 445 hours . A and C can do it in 4 hours . How long will B alone take to do it ?
questions.explanation:
LCM (6,445,4)\(= 24\ units\)

Let total work to be done be 24 units.

Work done by ;

A in a day \(= \ \frac{24}{6} = \ 4\ units—(1)\)

B+C in a day \(= \ \frac{24 \times 5}{24} = \ 5\ units–(2)\)

A+C in a day \(= \ \frac{24}{4} = \ 6\ units—(3)\)

Putting (1) in (3);

\(4 + C = 6\)

\( C = \ 2\ units\)

Putting C in (2);

\(2 + B = 5\)

\( B\  = \ 3\ units\)

Time taken by B to complete the work \(= \ \frac{24}{3} = \ 8\ hours\)

questions.question: A can do a work in 15 days while B can do it in 20 days. If both work for 5 days. What part of work has been done?
questions.explanation:
Given A can complete the work in 15 days ,while B can complete the work in 20 days .

The total work is 60 units . [We should always take the LCM of time taken by each workers as Total work to ease the calculation ]

Now calculate the efficiencies of A and B .

We know, Efficiency = Total work/ Total time taken to complete it 

Efficiency of A = \(\frac{60}{15}\)=4 unit /day

Efficiency of B = \(\frac{60}{20}\) =3 unit /day

And if they work together , resultant efficiency = (4+3)=7 units/ day

Given ,they both work together for 5 days .

So the total work done will be 5× 7= 35 unit

So , in fraction we can say the work done = \(\frac{35}{60} =\)\(\frac{7}{12}\)

\(\)

questions.question: Lakshmi can do a piece of work in 6 days, but with the help of her friend Taapsee, she can do it in 4 days. In what time Taapsee can do it alone?
questions.explanation:
Laksmi’s one day’s work = 16

Laksmi’s and Taapsee’s one day’s work = 14

Taapsee’s one day’s work = 14-16=112

Taapsee can do it alone in 12 days.

questions.question: (P + Q) can do a piece of work in 30 days and P can do same work in 90 days. In how many days will Q do this work ?
questions.explanation:
\(\frac{1}{P} + \frac{1}{Q} =\) \(\frac{1}{30}\)

\(= > \frac{1}{90} + \frac{1}{Q} = \frac{1}{30}\)

\(= > \frac{1}{Q} = \frac{1}{30} - \frac{1}{90}\)

\(= > \frac{1}{Q} = \frac{2}{90} = \frac{1}{45}\)

\(= > Q\  = \ 45\ \)

Option '45 days' is the correct answer.

questions.question: Luv and Kush working together can complete a work in 3 days. If Luv alone completes the same work in 5 days. In how many days Kush alone can complete the same work?
questions.explanation:
Luv and Kush  together can complete the task in 3 days.

So, in one day, they will complete 1/3 part of the task.

Therefore, (Luv + Kush)'s one day work will be = 1/3

Similarly, Luv's one day work = 1/5

Therefore, Kush's one day work = 13-15=215

In one day Kush completes the 2/15 part of the work so he will complete the entire work in 152=7.5 days.

questions.question: 7 men can complete a work in 12 days. They started the work and after 7 days, two men left. In how many days will the work be completed by the remaining men ?
questions.explanation:
Let efficiency of 1 man be 1 unit.

Total work to be done \(= \ 7 \times 12\  = \ 84\ units\)

Work done in 5 days by 7 men \(= \ 7 \times 7 = 49\ units\)

Remaining work \(= \ 84 - 49 = \ 35\ units\)

After 2 men left,

Time taken by 5 men to do the remaining work\(= \ \frac{35}{5} = \ 7\ days\)

questions.question: 18 women can complete a work in 52 days, then find how many women will be required to complete half of the same work in 36 days?
questions.explanation:
Let work done by women in 1 day be 1 unit.

Total work to be done \(= \ 18 \times 52\ units\)

Let x be women required.

As per question;

\(\frac{1}{2} \times 18 \times 52 = \ (x)36\)

\(= > x\  = \ 13\ \)

Option d

questions.question: Sita and Gita can do a work in 30 days and 50 days respectively. Sita started the work and left after 3 days. Gita took over and completed the work. In how many days was the total work completed?
questions.explanation:
LCM(30,50) = 150 ( Total work )

Sita’s one day’s work= 5

Sita’s 3 day’s work = 15

Work left= 150 - 15 = 135

Gita's one day’s work= 3

Gita's can do work in = 1353=45 days

So total days = 45+3 = 48 days

Alternate Method:

Sita can do the work in 30 days → 1 day work = 1/30
Gita can do the work in 50 days → 1 day work = 1/50
Sita works for 3 days, then Gita completes the remaining work
We need: Total days to complete the work
Work done by Sita in 3 days
Sita’s 1 day work = 1/30
Work done in 3 days = 3 × 1/30 = 3/30 = 1/10
Remaining work
Remaining work = 1 - 1/10 = 9/10
Time for Gita to finish remaining work
Gita’s 1 day work = 1/50
Time = Remaining work ÷ Gita’s 1 day work
Time = (9/10) ÷ (1/50) = (9/10) × 50 = 45 days
Total time
Total time = Sita’s 3 days + Gita’s 45 days = 48 days
Answer:
Total work was completed in 48 days

questions.question: P and Q together can do a piece of work in 30 days. While Q and R together can do the same work in 40 days, and R and P together can do it in 24 days. In how many days will this work be completed by P, Q, and R working alone, respectively?
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Time taken by P and Q together = 30 days
• Time taken by Q and R together = 40 days
• Time taken by R and P together = 24 days

Calculation:
Let total work be the LCM of 30, 40, and 24
Total work = LCM(30, 40, 24) = 120 units
Efficiency of (P + Q) = 120 / 30 = 4 units/day
Efficiency of (Q + R) = 120 / 40 = 3 units/day
Efficiency of (R + P) = 120 / 24 = 5 units/day
2 × (Efficiency of P + Q + R) = 4 + 3 + 5 = 12 units/day
Efficiency of (P + Q + R) = 12 / 2 = 6 units/day
Efficiency of P = 6 - 3 = 3 units/day
Efficiency of Q = 6 - 5 = 1 unit/day
Efficiency of R = 6 - 4 = 2 units/day
Time taken by P alone = 120 / 3 = 40 days
Time taken by Q alone = 120 / 1 = 120 days
Time taken by R alone = 120 / 2 = 60 days

Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.question: 16 men take 24 days to complete a job working 6 hours a day. The number of hours a day should 32 men take to complete the job in 12 days?
questions.explanation:
Total work to be done \(= \ 16 \times 24 \times 6\  = 2304\ units\)

Since, work done remains same.Therefore;

Number of hours requires \(= \ \frac{2304}{32 \times 12}\  = 6\ hours\)

questions.question: 15 men can finish a job in x days. If 5 extra Men join them, the job takes (x-10) days . What is the value of x?
questions.explanation:
Let efficiency of every man be 1 unit.

Total work done by 15 men in x days \(= \ 15x\ units\)

Now; when 5 extra men joined

\(15x\  = \ 20 \times (x - 10)\)

\(= > 15x = 20x - 200\)

\(= > 5x = 200\)

\(= > x\  = \ 40\ \)

questions.question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 10 days, B and C together can complete the same work in 15 days and A and C together can do the same work in 30 days, then find the total number of days required to complete the work when all A, B and C are working together.
questions.explanation:
LCM ( 10,15,30) \(= \ 60\ \)

Let work to be done be 60 units

Work done by A+B in 1 day\(= \ \frac{60}{10} = \ 6\ units\)

Work done by B+C in 1 day\(= \ \frac{60}{15}\  = \ 4\ units\)

Work done by A+C in 1 day\(= \ \frac{60}{30}\  = \ 2\ units\)

Work done by A+B+C in 1 day \(\  = \ \frac{10}{2} = \ 5\ units\)

Time taken by all of three of them \(= \ \frac{60}{6}\  = 10\ days\)

questions.question: A and B undertake a piece of work for Rs 600. A can do it in 30 days and B can do it in 60 days. With the help of C , they finish it in 10 days. How much should C be paid for her contribution?
questions.explanation:
LCM(30,60)=60

Let work done be 60 units.

Work done by A in 1 day\(= \frac{60}{30} = 2\ units\)

Work done by B in 1 day \(= \frac{60}{60} = 1\ units\)

Let work done by C in 1 day be x units.

As per question;

\(10(2 + 1 + x) = 60\)

\(= > x = 3\ units\)

Efficiency ratio of A:B:C\(= 2:1:3\)

C’s share\(= \ \frac{3}{6} \times 600 = Rs\ 300\)

questions.question: 13 men working 8 hours a day can complete a work in 18 days. How many hours per day must 16 men work to complete the same work in 26 days?
questions.explanation:
Total work done by 13 men \(= \ 13 \times 8 \times 18\  = 1872\ units\)

As, work done will be the same.

Therefore,

Hours required \(= \ \frac{1872}{(16 \times 26)} = 4.5\ hours\)

questions.question: 12 Women are working for 5 hours a day, completing work in 15 days. If 13 more women joined and all women are working for four hours a day, then in how many days would the work be completed?

Option b

questions.question: 15 men can do a work in 20 days while 10 womens can do the same work in 25 days . in how many days 6 mens & 5 womens together can do the same work?

let total work be 1500 units

questions.question: 15 men can do a piece of work in 15 days. Then 25 men can do twice the work in how many days if they are working with 20 % less efficiency ?
questions.explanation:
Let the efficiency in first case be 5 unit

Then the efficiency in second case = 4 unit (20% less)

\(\frac{m1 \times d1 \times e1}{w1}\) = \(\frac{m2 \times d2 \times e2}{w2}\)

\(\Rightarrow\)\(\frac{15 \times 15 \times 5}{1}\) = \(\frac{25 \times d2 \times 4}{2}\)

\(\Rightarrow\)\(d2 = 22\frac{1}{2}\) days

questions.question: 16 men or 32 women can do a piece of work in 48 days. The ratio of the efficiency of man and boy is 3:2. In how many days will 25 men, 8 women and 16 boys do the work?
questions.explanation:

∴1 man’s work = \(\frac{1}{768}\)

According to the question:

Boy’s work for 1 day = 1768×23=22304=11152

\(\Rightarrow \frac{25}{768} + \frac{1}{192}\)+\(\frac{1}{72}\) = \(\frac{119}{2304}\)

Number of days they will take = 2304119

questions.question: Ajay can do a piece of work in 24 days and Sunil can do a piece of work in 8 days if they work on alternative days with Ajay beginning the work, then in how many days the work will be completed?
questions.explanation:
Given Information:

  • Ajay can do the work in 24 days
  • Sunil can do the work in 8 days
  • They work on alternative days
  • Ajay starts first

Calculation:

If A can do piece of work in ‘n’ days and B can do piece of work in ‘m’ days, then both together can complete the work in:

=2(m×n)m+n

No. of days they work together is:

=2(24×8)24+8

= 12 days

So, Ajay and Sunil can complete the work in 12 days.

questions.question: 10 male labours can finish the work in 36 days and 20 female laborers can finish the same work in 24 days. If all of them work together, then in how many days will they finish the same work?
questions.explanation:
Let work done by male and female labours be m and w units respectively.

\(10m \times 36 = 20w \times 24\)

\( 360m = 480w\)

\( m = \frac{4w}{3}\)

Let efficiency of women \(= w = \ 3\ units.\ \)

Then, efficiency of men\(\  = \ m = 4/3 \times 3 = \ 4\ units\)

Total work to be done\(= \ 10m \times 36 = 360m = 1440\ units\)

Time taken by all of them \(= \frac{\ 1440}{\lbrack 10(4) + 20(3)\rbrack}\)

\(= \frac{1440}{100} = \frac{72}{5}{\ days}\)

questions.question: 18 men take 9 days to complete a piece of work. They worked for a period of 4 days. After that, they were joined by 2 more men. How many more days will be taken by them to complete the remaining Work?
questions.explanation:

Total work =18×9=162

Work done by 18 men in 4 days\(\  = \ 18 \times 4 = 72\ units\)

Let days taken by them be x.

Work left\(\  = \ 162 - 72 = 90\)

\(= > 20 \times x = 90\)

\(= > x = 4.5\ days\)

the job done by Aditi = P

the job done by Nimisha = Q

the job done by Rajni = R

\(\frac{1}{P} = \frac{5\  - \ 4}{120}\)

P = 120 hours

Therefore, part of job done by Aditi in 40 hours =  \(\frac{40}{120}\  = \frac{\ 1}{3}\)part

questions.question: Ajay and Bunty together can complete a piece of work in 28 days while Bunty and Chandani together can complete the same work in 20 days. Ajay worked on it for 6 days, Bunty worked on it for 16 days and Chandani completed rest of the work in 20 days. Find the time taken by Ajay to complete the whole work.
questions.explanation:
Let total amount of work is 140 units (LCM of 20 and 28)

Amount of work completed by Ajay and Bunty together in one day = 14028 = 5 units

Amount of work completed by Bunty and Chandani together in one day = 14020 = 7 units

Amount of work completed by Ajay and Bunty together in 6 days = 6 × 5 = 30 units

Amount of work completed by Bunty and Chandani together in 10 days = 10 × 7 = 70 units

Remaining work (140 – 30 – 70 = 40 units) is completed by Chandani in 10 days

So, efficiency of Chandani = 4010 = 4 units per day

Efficiency of Bunty = 7 – 4 = 3 units per day

Efficiency of Ajay = 5 – 3 = 2 units per day

Time taken by Ajay to complete the whole work = 1402 = 70 days

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 20 days while B alone can do it in 30 days. They work together for 5 days and the rest of the work is done by C in 2 days. If they get Rs 1500 for the whole work, B gets Rs x and E gets Rs.2x for doing some other work ,then find the amount earned by E?

Part of work done by B \(= \ 2 \times \frac{5}{60} = \frac{1}{6}\)

Part of work done by C =1-14-16=712

Ratio of share of A:B:C=14:16:712=3:2:7 

B’s share,x \(= \ \frac{2}{12} \times 1500 = Rs\ 250\)

E’s share \(= \ Rs\ 250 \times 2\  = \ Rs\ 500\)

questions.question: 15 men working 8 hours a day take 40 days to manufacture 18000 articles. If 5 men left the work after 25 days, then how much additional time is required to finish the work?
questions.explanation:
Number of articles manufactured by 15 men working 8 hours a day in 25 days = 18000 × \(\frac{25}{40}\) = 11,250

Remaining articles to be manufactured = 18000 – 11250 = 6750 articles

Let the efficiency of each worker be ‘E’ articles/day

So, 15 × 8 × 40 × E = 18000

Or, E = 3.75

Let the number of days taken by 10 workers to make 6750 articles be ‘d’ days

So, {6750\(\div\)(3.75 × 10 × 8)} = d

Or, d = 22.5

So, additional days are required to finish the work = 22.5 days

Hence, option C.

questions.question: 144 units of work can be completed by ‘A’ alone in 24 days. ‘A’ started working alone and joined ‘B’ after 10 days such that they completed the remaining work in 6 days. Find the number of days taken by ‘B’ to complete the whole work alone.
questions.explanation:
Let the efficiency of B = ‘x’ units/day

Efficiency of A = (144\(\div\)24) = 6 units/day

According to the question:

6 × 10 + (6 + x) × 6 = 144

Or, 60 + 36 + 6x = 144

Or, 6x = 144 – 96

Or, 6x = 48

Or, x = 8

Number of days taken by ‘B’ to complete the work alone = (144\(\div\)8) = 18 days

questions.question: 15 men can do a piece of work in 12 days and 30 women can do the same work in 12 days. If the work is started by 5 men and 6 women and they work for 10 days after that all the remaining work is done by 5 men. How many days in total are required to complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Let work done by men and women in 1 day be m and w units respectively.

As per ques;

Total work to be done =  15m ×12  = 180m/units

Since, total work to be done will be equal by men and women.Therefore;

\(180m = 30w \times 12\)

\(= > m:w = 2:1\)

Now,

Let days taken by 5 men be k days.

Let work done by man m= 2 units and women w=1 unit in 1 day Total work to be done\(= \ 180m = 360\ units\)

As per question;

\(10(5m + 6w) + 5m(k) = 360\)

\(= > 10(16) + 10k = 360\)

\(= > 10k = 200\)

\(= > k = 20\ days\)

questions.question: 7 men together can build a bridge in 45 days. A woman is 12.5% less efficient than a man. If 5 women and 2 men work together on building a bridge for 35 days and the remaining bridge is build by one man and one woman together, then find the ratio of total work done by men to that by women, once the whole bridge is build.
questions.explanation:
Let the efficiency of a man = 8y units/day

Then, the total work to be done in building the bridge = 8y × 7 × 45 = 2520y units

Efficiency of a woman = 8y × 0.875 = 7y units/day

Combined efficiency of 5 women and 2 men = 5 × 7y + 2 × 8y = 51y units/day

Work done by 5 women and 2 men in 35 days = 51y × 35 = 1785y units

Remaining work = 2520y – 1785y = 735y units

So, number of days taken by 1 man and 1 woman together to complete the remaining work = 735 ÷ (8 + 7) = 49 days

So, total work done by women = 35y × 35 + 7y × 49 = 1225y + 343y = 1568y units

Total work done by men = 2520y – 1568y = 952y units

So, required ratio = 952y : 1568y = 17:28

Hence, option A.

questions.question: Ananya and Vaishali together can do a piece of work in 12 days, Vaishali and Sahivani together can do it in 18 days. If Ananya and Vaishali started the work and Ananya left after 4 days. Then Sahivani joined Vaishali and Vaishali left on the 6th day of the work. Sahivani finished it working for 17 days, then in how many days can Ananya alone finish the work?
questions.explanation:
Sahivani worked alone for 15 days (because for the first 2 days he worked with Vaishali), Ananya and Vaishali worked together for 4 days and Vaishali and Sahivani together worked for 2 days.

So total work done by Ananya and Vaishali in 4 days = 4 × 112=  13

So total work done by Vaishali and Sahivani in 2 days =  2 × 118= 19

So the total work done by Sahivani in 15 days = 1-13-19=59

So work done by Sahivani in 1 day = =5915=127

So Sahivani can do the whole work in 27 days.

It is given that Vaishali and Sahivani together can do the work in 18 days

Hence work done by Vaishali in one day = 118 - 127 = 154

Means Vaishali can complete in 54 days.

Similarly Ananya and Vaishali can finish the work in 12 days.

So work done by Ananya in one day = 112-154=7108

Hence Ananya can complete the work in 1087 days

questions.question: Aman and Atul together can do a work in 15 days. If Aman increases his efficiency by 3313% while Atul decreases his efficiency to 75%, then the time required by them together to do the same work remains the same. Find the time taken by Aman alone to do the amount of work which Atul can do alone in 12 days.
questions.explanation:
Let the efficiency of Aman and Atul be ‘x’ units per day and ‘y’ units per day, respectively.

 1x + 1y = 115

Or, (x + y) = xy15 …………. (I)

Also, 34x + 43y = 115

Or, 9y + 16x = 12 × xy15………… (II)

On combining equation (I) and (II), we have;

9y + 16x = 12 × (x + y)

Or, 9y + 16x = 12x + 12y

Or, 4x = 3y

So,  xy = 34 

Since, ratio of efficiencies of Aman to that of Atul is 3:4. So, the ratio of time taken by Aman and Atul to do a particular work will be 4:3, respectively.

So, required time = 12 × 43 = 16 days

questions.question: A and B together can complete a work in ‘t’ minutes and B and C together can complete the same work in ‘3t’ minutes. If the ratio of A’s efficiency to C’s efficiency is 6: 1, then in what time A alone can complete the work?
questions.explanation:
Since, ratio of A’s efficiency to C’s efficiency is 6: 1.

So, let the time taken by A alone and C alone to complete the work is ‘x’ minutes and ‘6x’ minutes.

From the question:

\(\frac{1}{x}\  + \ \frac{1}{B}\  = \ \frac{1}{t}\) --------------(1)

And,

\(\frac{1}{B}\  + \ \frac{1}{6x}\  = \ \frac{1}{3t}\) --------------(2)

From equations (1) and (2):

\(\frac{1}{x}\  - \ \frac{1}{6x}\  = \ \frac{1}{t}\  - \ \frac{1}{3t}\)

\(\frac{5}{6x}\  = \ \frac{2}{3t}\)

\(x\  = \ \frac{5t}{4}\)

So, the time taken by A alone to complete the work = \(\frac{5t}{4}\) minutes

questions.question: 'A' and 'B' together can do some work in 7.5 days. If four days after starting the work, 'A' is replaced by 'C', then the work will be finished in 4 more days. If 'C' takes 25% more time to finish the work alone than that by A, then find the time taken by 'C' to finish the work alone.
questions.explanation:
Time taken by 'A' and 'B' to finish the full work together = 7.5 days

Let the total work be 30x units.

So, combined efficiency of 'A' and 'B' = (30x/7.5) = 4x units/day

So, work done by 'A' and 'B' together in 4 days = 4x × 4 = 16x units/day

So, remaining work = 30x - 16x = 14x units

So, the combined efficiency of 'B' and 'C' = 14x ÷ 4 = 3.5x units/day

Let 'A' and 'B' efficiencies be 'm' units/day and 'n' units/day.

Since ratio of time taken between 'A' and 'C' is 4:5, ratio of efficiency will be 5:4.

So, efficiency of 'C' = 0.8 × m = 0.8m

ATQ;

m + n = 4x .... (I)

0.8m + n = 3.5x .... (II)

On subtracting equation (II) from equation (I), we have;

0.2m = 0.5x

So, m = 2.5x

So, time taken by 'C' to finish the work alone = 30x ÷ (2.5x × 0.8) = 15 days

Hence, option b.

questions.question: 10 Men can do a piece of work in 12 days. 12 Women can do 40% of the same work in 8 days and 6 Children can do 75% of the same work in 12 days. If 4 Men, 6 Women and 2 Children start work alternately, then who will be the last to complete the work?
questions.explanation:
Given,

10 Men can do a piece of work in 12 days

=> 10 men = 12 days

So, 4 men = \(\frac{12\  \times 10}{4}\)

=> 4 men = 30 days

And, 12 Women can do 40% of the same work in 8 days (given)

=> 12 women = 40% in 8 days

=> 12 women = 80% in 16 days

=> 12 women = 100% in 20 days

So, 12 women = 20 days

Thus, 6 women = \(\frac{20\  \times 12}{6}\)

=> 6 women = 40 days

And, 6 Children can do 75% of the same work in 12 days

=> 6 children = 75% in 12 days

=> 6 children = 25% in 4 days

=> 6 children = 100% in 16 days

=> 6 children = 16 days

So, 2 children = \(\frac{16 \times 6}{2}\)

=> 2 children = 48 days

Total work = LCM of 30, 40 and 48 = 240

4 Men’s one day’s work = \(\frac{240}{30}\)

= \(8\) units

6 Women’s one day’s work = \(\frac{240}{40}\)

= \(6\) units

2 Child’s one day’s work = \(\frac{240}{48}\)

= 5 units

Total work of 3 days = 8 + 6 + 5 = 19 units

Total work of 36 days = 228

Now,

it’s 4 Men’s terms, they will complete 228 + 8

= 236 units

Then,

it’s 6 women’s terms

6 women will be the last to complete the work.

questions.question: (x-1) men and (x+2) women together can complete the work in 10 days. If 6 men can complete the work in 20 days and 12 women complete the work in 15 days, then find the value of x.
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• (x − 1) men + (x + 2) women finish work in 10 days
• 6 men finish work in 20 days
• 12 women finish work in 15 days

Calculation:
1 man’s work per day
= 1 ÷ (6 × 20) = 1/120

1 woman’s work per day
= 1 ÷ (12 × 15) = 1/180

Total work per day

(x − 1)/120 + (x + 2)/180 = 1/10

LCM 360

3(x − 1) + 2(x + 2) ÷ 360 = 1/10

3x − 3 + 2x + 4 = 36

5x + 1 = 36

5x = 35

x = 7

Final Answer: 7
Hence, option D is correct.

Used Concepts:
• Efficiency = 1 ÷ time
• Work = efficiency × time
• Linear equation

questions.question: (x + 2) men working 4 hours a day can complete (3/10)th of a work in 9 days. (x + 4) men working 3 hours a day can complete the remaining work in 20 days. What is the value of x?
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Number of men in first group (M1) = x + 2
• Hours per day for first group (H1) = 4 hours
• Days taken by first group (D1) = 9 days
• Work completed by first group (W1) = 3/10
• Number of men in second group (M2) = x + 4
• Hours per day for second group (H2) = 3 hours
• Days taken by second group (D2) = 20 days
• Work completed by second group (W2) = 1 - 3/10 = 7/10

Calculation:
Using the work formula: (M1 * D1 * H1) / W1 = (M2 * D2 * H2) / W2
[(x + 2) * 9 * 4] / (3/10) = [(x + 4) * 20 * 3] / (7/10)
[(x + 2) * 36] / 3 = [(x + 4) * 60] / 7
12 * (x + 2) = [60 * (x + 4)] / 7
Multiply both sides by 7:
84 * (x + 2) = 60 * (x + 4)
Divide both sides by 12:
7 * (x + 2) = 5 * (x + 4)
7x + 14 = 5x + 20
2x = 6
x = 3

Hence, option (A) is correct.

Used Concepts:
• Time and Work Formula
• Ratio and Proportion

questions.question: (n + 1) men working 9 hours a day can complete 30% of a work in 4 days. (n + 3) men working 6 hours a day can complete the remaining work in 10 days. What is the value of n?
questions.explanation:
Time taken by (n+1) to complete 100% of work \(= \ (n + 1) \times 9 \times 4 \times \frac{10}{3}\)

Time taken by (n+3) to complete 100% of work\(= (n + 3) \times 6 \times 10 \times \frac{10}{7}\)

Since work done will be equal.

\(= > \ (n + 1) \times 9 \times 4 \times \frac{10}{3} = (n + 3) \times 6 \times 10 \times \frac{10}{7}\)

\(= > 12(n + 1) = \frac{60}{7}(n + 3)\)

\(= > 84n + 84 = 60n + 180\)

\(= > 24n = 96\)

\(= > n = 4\)

questions.question: (a + 3) men working 12 hours a day can complete 30% of a work in 3 days. (a + 5) men working 5 hours a day can complete the remaining work in 12 days. What is the value of a?
questions.explanation:
Total time taken by (a+3) men to complete 100 % of work

\(= \ \frac{\lbrack(a + 3) \times 12 \times 3\rbrack}{0.3} - - (1)\)

Total time taken by (a+5) men to complete 100 % of work

\(\  = \ \frac{\lbrack(a + 5) \times 12 \times 5\rbrack}{0.7} - - - (2)\)

From (1) and (2)

\(\frac{\lbrack(a + 3) \times 12 \times 3\rbrack}{0.3} = \frac{\{\lbrack(a + 5) \times 12 \times 5\rbrack}{0.7}\)

\(= > 7a + 21 = 5a + 25\)

\(= > 2a = 4\)

\(= > a = 2\)

questions.question: 14 men and 12 women together can complete a piece of work in 8 days and work done by a woman in one day is half the work done by a man in one day. If 8 men and 4 women started working and after 5 days 3 men left the work and 8 new women joined then, in how many more days will the work be completed?
questions.explanation:
Let work done by women be 2 units respectively.

Work done by men in 1 day\(\  = \ 4\ units\)

Total work to be done\(= \ (14(4) + 12(2))8 = 640\ units\)

Work done by 8 men and 4 women in 5 days

\(= \ 5\lbrack 8(4) + 4(2)\rbrack = 200\ units\)

Work lef\(t\  = \ 640\  - 200\  = \ 440\ units\)

Men left\(\  = \ 8 - 3\  = \ 5\)

Time taken by 5 men and 12 women \(\  = \frac{440}{\lbrack 5(4) + 12(2)\rbrack}\)

\(= \frac{440}{44} = 10\ days\)

questions.question: X men can finish a work in Y days. 0.3X women can finish 1/5th of the same work in (Y-10) days. If 0.3X women can complete 1/3rd of the work in 30 days. Find 0.5X men can finish 1/2 of the same work in how many days?
questions.explanation:

0.3X women can complete the whole work in = 5(Y − 10) days

0.3X women complete the same work in = 30 × 3 = 90 days

So, 0.3X × 5(Y − 10) = 0.3X × 90

Y – 10 =18

Y = 28 days

If A men complete the work in 28 days, then

0.5X men complete 1/2nd work in = 28×12÷12= 28 days

questions.question: ‘A’ men can finish a work in T days. 0.4A women can finish 1/2 of the same work in (T-6) days. If 0.6A women can complete 1/2 of the work in 36 days. Find 0.3A men can finish 1/3rd of the same work in how many days?

0.4A women can complete the whole work in = 2(T − 6) days

So, 0.4A ×2(T − 6) = 0.6A × 72

B – 6 = 54

B = 60 days

If A men complete the work in 60 days, then 0.3A men complete 1/3rd work in = 60×103×13 = 66.67 days

questions.question:
S and Q together can finish a work in 24 days, Q and T together can do the same work in ‘x’ days while S and T together can do that work in \(\frac{120}{7}\) days. If all 3 of them can do that work in \(\frac{40}{3}\) days. Which of the following is the correct order of time taken by S, Q, and T alone to finish the work?

A: (x + 10) days

B: 2x days

C: 3x days
questions.explanation:
Let time taken by S, Q, and T together to finish the work is ‘s’, ‘q’, and ‘t’ respectively.

According to the question:

\(\frac{1}{s} + \frac{1}{q} = \frac{1}{24}...........(1)\)

\(\frac{1}{q} + \frac{1}{t} = \frac{1}{x}...........(2)\)

\(\frac{1}{s} + \frac{1}{t} = \frac{7}{120}...........(3)\)

\(\frac{1}{s} + \frac{1}{q} + \frac{1}{t} = \frac{3}{40}...........(4)\)

From (1) and (4):

\(\frac{1}{24} + \frac{1}{t} = \frac{3}{40}\)

\(\frac{1}{t} = \frac{3}{40} - \frac{1}{24} = \frac{9 - 5}{120}\)

t = 30 days

From (3) and (4):

\(\frac{7}{120} + \frac{1}{q} = \frac{3}{40}\)

\(\frac{1}{q} = \frac{3}{40} - \frac{7}{120} = \frac{9 - 7}{120}\)

q = 60 days

From equation (2):

\(\frac{1}{60} + \frac{1}{30} = \frac{1}{x}\)

\(\frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{60} + \frac{1}{30} = \frac{1 + 2}{60} = \frac{3}{60}\)

x = 20

From equation (1):

\(\frac{1}{s} + \frac{1}{60} = \frac{1}{24}\)

\(\frac{1}{s} = \frac{1}{24} - \frac{1}{60} = \frac{5 - 2}{120} = \frac{3}{120}\)

s = 40

Time taken by S alone = 40 days = 2x days

Time taken by Q alone = 60 days = 3x days

Time taken by T alone = 30 = (x + 10) days

Hence, the correct order is BCA.

questions.question: A contractor agreed to make M km road in Z days. He employed 0.7Z workers for this work. After 60 days, he realized that only 0.25Z km of road had been completed. Z2 – 206Z + 1200 = 0

Hence answer is option C

B = P started the work at Z am and finish it at 7 pm on same day, while Q started the same work on next day at Z am and finish it 3 pm. One day P started the work alone and left the work at 2pm, so Q finished the remaining work till 5 pm. Time taken by P alone to finish the work is (N5– 6) hours. Find the value of N

questions.question:
Time taken by P, Q, and R together to complete the job is 37.5% less than time taken by Q and R together to complete the job, while P and Q together can do the job in Z days, and R alone can complete it in Y days. Share of R is Rs. 8000 out of total share of P, Q, and R together (Rs. 16000). Find the Value of Y2, if P, Q and R together can complete the job in (Z – K) days.

Which of the following is/are definitely true. 

I. Y2= K

II. If time taken by P, Q and R together to complete the job is 15 day less than that of P and Q together, then time taken by S to complete the job is 20 days, if Z is half efficient that as that of S.   

III. Z = Y
questions.explanation:
Ratio of time taken of (P + Q + R) and (Q + R) = 5:8

Ratio of efficiency of (P + Q + R) to that of (Q + R) = 8:5

So, efficiency of P = 8 – 5 = 3 units/day 

Share of R out of total share = 800016000=12 

That means efficiency of R = (P + Q)

Efficiency of R = P + Q = 82 = 4 units/day 

So, efficiency of Q = 4 – 3 = 1 unit/day 

Time taken by P and Q together to complete the job = Z days 

Time taken by P, Q, and R together to complete the job = (Z – K) days 

Now, 

Z = 2 × (Z – K)

Value of Z = 2K 

So, time taken by P and Q together to complete the job = 2K days = time taken by R alone to complete the job = Y. 

I. Y2 = K

Value of Z = 2K 

Also, Y = Z 

So, Y2 = K 

This statement is true. 

II. If time taken by P, Q and R together to complete the job is 15 day less than that of P and Q together, then time taken by S to complete the job is 20 days, if Z is half efficient that as that of S. 

Value of K = 15

So, Z = Y = 2 × 15 = 30 

S is twice efficient as that of R, so time taken by S to complete the job is = 302 = 15 days. 

This statement is false. 

III. Z = Y

This statement is true. 

So, only I and III are true, 

Hence, the answer is option B

questions.question: P, Q, and R together can complete the job in 5Z days. All three together started the work and after K days R left, remaining work complete by P and Q together in Y days. Time taken by Q to complete the job alone is 20% less than that of P. If total amount of Rs. 24M gets by P, Q, and R together to complete the job, then find difference between share of P and R. Combined work of P and Q is 60% of total work.
questions.explanation:
P and Q together do 60% of total work, so R alone does 40% of total work. 

Share of money distribution is same as ratio of amount of work done. 

Q and P work for same number of days, so ratio of work done = ratio of their efficiency = 

Share of (P + Q) = 60% × 24M = 14.4M 

Share of R = 40% × 24M = 9.6M 

Ratio of time taken of P and Q = 5:4

Ratio of efficiency of P and Q = 4:5 

Share of P = 49× 14.4M = 6.4M

Required difference = 9.6M – 6.4M = 3.2M

Hence answer is option A
